correctness.rationale: The distributional heat equation yields the displayed exact F derivative; strict convexity of logcosh(az)-z gives precisely one positive zero for a>1 and none for a<=1. Differentiating the normal CDF gives a single P optimum precisely for d>L and the touching discontinuity at d=L. Layer-cake integration, strict decrease of x/artanh(x), and derivative signs at s_P and d^2 prove s_P<s_F<d^2. The small-threshold asymptotic follows from an exact logcosh expansion. Standalone quadrature, normal-moment, finite-difference and randomized sign checks passed but are not substitutes for the proof.

evidence: Rudolf 2018 doi:10.1111/1365-2656.12850 provides known qualitative nonlinear variation-versus-interaction effects in experiments and simulations.
Weis et al. 2014 doi:10.1111/jeb.12465 shows flowering-date variance can change assortative mating, not the present Gaussian expected overlap duration.
Montes-Perez et al. 2025 doi:10.1002/ecm.70046 measures overlap days and interaction frequencies in 8-year observations without a variance optimization theorem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These sources cover ecologically broader phenomena but none of the inspected arguments implies the exact all-parameter Gaussian fixed-duration onset-variance result. Prior qualitative claims of nonlinear overlap response are excluded from claimed novelty.

evidence: Austin 2024 establishes observed reassembly and changed durations, not an all-separation theorem on Gaussian onset variance.
Rudolf 2018 establishes nonlinear effects of altered variation in other interaction models and cannot determine the present exact constants.

Buckley 2021 treats a different overlap sampling/abundance model; Stemkovski 2023 optimizes overlap between skew-normal *densities*, not uniform fixed-duration intervals shifted by Gaussian year effects.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: No inspected prior theorem is stronger in the relevant hypothesis class or yields the exact \(d=L/2\) and \(d=L\) cutoffs as a corollary. The distinction between probability of any overlap and average days is not resolved by the cited ecological empirical results. Classical Gaussian heat-kernel facts alone require the additional complete sign and optimizer analysis supplied here.

evidence: Austin et al. 2024 doi:10.1111/nph.19994 defines actual days/relative proportion of flowering overlap; Buckley et al. 2021 doi:10.1111/1365-2656.13451 defines duration and area-based overlap, not a Gaussian two-window stochastic model.
The exact random-interval quantity equals Gaussian convolution of a triangular tent, a standard transformation used in the proof.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Re-expressed the exact claim as Gaussian heat evolution of a triangular tent, and also as a layer-cake average of normal interval probabilities. Inspected ecologically equivalent overlap definitions and mathematical search terms; inspected texts do not establish the half-duration threshold and two-metric separation. The Gaussian convolution identity itself is standard and is not an original claim.

evidence: Austin et al. 2024 reports field/herbarium posterior summaries and pairwise flowering-overlap estimates, not a Gaussian variance parameter table.
Buckley et al. 2021 tabulates responses of three phenological-overlap metrics to climate and community factors, without the two exact thresholds.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Checked the relevant article tabulations and searched the same exact pairwise objectives for a known closed-form threshold/optimum table. The materials inspected provide observational estimates, not the classified mathematical invariant.

originality.rationale: The new assertion is the joint exact all-separation classification of Gaussian relative-onset variability for expected co-flowering days versus probability of any co-flowering, with distinct sharp thresholds, unique optimizers, onset asymptotics and strict optimizer ordering. Inspected ecological papers treat empirical co-flowering, non-Gaussian phenomenology or different floral/mating objectives. Prior standard normal smoothing and variation arguments are credited; priority remains provisional with classical random-interval theory as a residual risk.
residual_risks: Equivalent sharp Gaussian triangular-convolution optimum may be present in older random-interval, reliability or heat-kernel literature outside the inspected corpus.
The assumptions intentionally exclude variable flowering durations, skewness and environmental covariance; empirical effect sizes may not transfer.
Historical priority and ecological generalization have not been independently assessed.

value.rationale: Duration of phenological co-occurrence and occurrence of any overlap are both directly measured ecological quantities, and earlier long-term work emphasizes heterogeneous timing shifts. This result shows they can respond in strictly opposite directions to timing variability, with two different sharp geometry thresholds and distinct global maximizers. It supplies a reproducible exact benchmark for interpreting Gaussian year-to-year phenological mismatch; it makes no calibrated fitness or climate intervention claim.
